description: Supervisor-owned immutable symbol identities for actor-isolated Atto runtimes

source_syntax.global_semantics: Only declared and resolved exported/core symbols enter the process/tenant global registry. A bare literal remains isolate-local unless resolved to such a declaration.
source_syntax.visibility: Import/export resolution is required for userland global references. A symbol identity grants no access permissions.

identity.global_placement: supervisor/runtime-owned immutable registry, never in an actor heap
native_representations: read-only interned data, optionally shared read-only mapping
identity.wasm_representation: host-owned tenant registry with structured-clone-safe value handle
identity.lifecycle: tenant or process lifetime; no slot reuse while handles can exist
identity.wire_format: Do not send bare process-local handles between processes; encode qualified symbol spelling and re-intern at receiving runtime
identity.hot_reload: Preexisting canonical identity survives module reload; unloading does not recycle a live symbol ID
identity.aot: Compile exported/core symbols into a sorted immutable descriptor table; initialize/link prior to actor start
identity.thread_safety: Concurrent intern publication is linearizable; readers see fully initialized immutable entries

negative_requirements: No actor-owned pointer or mutable heap allocation crosses the symbol boundary
No raw JavaScript Symbol is sent via postMessage
No hash-only identity, hash collision aliasing, ID recycling, or partially published interning
No actor may bypass compiler import visibility by fabricating a global spelling
No local symbol may resolve in another actor's isolate context
No unbounded dynamic intern allocation or unchecked integer wraparound
No process-local symbol handle is treated as globally meaningful across processes or tenants
No inheritance of symbol identity across supervisor restart without explicit re-interning
